commitResults.messageTitle: Duke.java: Greet user and exit with BOT identity
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-0 requirement: print a banner, greet the user
by name, and print a goodbye message on exit. Renamed the chatbot
from Duke to BOT and updated the ASCII banner to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Duke.java: Echo user commands until bye
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-1 requirement: read input in a loop and echo
each line back inside a divider block, exiting on the bye command.
Also switches to the indented divider/text format (4-space divider,
5-space text) for consistency across greet, echo, and exit output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Duke.java: Store and list user-entered tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-2 requirement: any input other than "list" or
"bye" is stored in a fixed-size array (capacity 100) and acknowledged
with "added: <text>"; "list" displays all stored items numbered.
No persistence to disk is needed at this stage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark/unmark commands and extract Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-3 requirement: tasks can be marked done/not done
via "mark N" / "unmark N", and "list" now shows each task's status
icon. Extracted task state into a separate Task class (description,
isDone, getStatusIcon/markAsDone/markAsNotDone) per the A-Classes
extension, replacing the raw String[] storage in Duke.java.

Also ignore *.class files in .gitignore in case javac is run without
-d (compiling straight into src/main/java).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add test-ui skill and UI test plan; wire into AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a project skill (.claude/skills/test-ui) that builds Duke, runs
the console test cases recorded in test/ui-test-plan.md against it,
prints a transcript of each session, and stops immediately on the
first mismatch, reporting expected vs. actual output.

test/ui-test-plan.md currently covers: greet-and-exit, listing with
no tasks, adding a todo/deadline/event and listing them, and
mark/unmark. Manually walked through the skill's procedure end to end
and all 4 test cases pass against the current implementation.

AGENTS.md now instructs that after any src/main/java change, the test
plan should be updated if behavior changed, and the test-ui skill
should be invoked before considering the change complete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Todo, Deadline, and Event task subclasses
commitResults.messageBody:
Each extends Task and overrides toString() to prepend its type icon
([T]/[D]/[E]) via super.toString(), per the A-Inheritance extension:
task-specific state (Deadline's "by", Event's "from"/"to") lives only
on the subclass, while shared description/done-status stays in Task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Duke.java: Support todo, deadline, and event commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds parsing for "todo <desc>", "deadline <desc> /by <when>", and
"event <desc> /from <start> /to <end>", storing them polymorphically
in the existing Task[] array. Each addition prints a confirmation
with the task's string form and the running task count. Replaces the
old catch-all free-text add from Level-2/3, which the Level-4 command
set no longer uses.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add error handling with a custom BotException
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-5 requirement (A-Exceptions extension): command
dispatch now validates input and throws BotException with a specific,
actionable message for an unrecognized command, a todo/deadline/event
missing its description or /by //from //to arguments, and a mark/unmark
with a missing, non-numeric, or out-of-range task number. Errors are
caught in main and printed inside the usual divider block instead of
crashing or silently doing nothing.

Adds Test Case 5 to test/ui-test-plan.md covering these error paths;
ran the test-ui skill and all 5 test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command and switch to ArrayList<Task>
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the Level-6 requirement: "delete N" removes the Nth task
and reports its final state plus the new running task count, reusing
the existing parseTaskIndex validation shared with mark/unmark. Per
the A-Collections extension, task storage moves from a fixed-size
Task[100] to an ArrayList<Task>, removing the 100-task cap.

Updates test/ui-test-plan.md: adds Test Case 6 for the delete
happy path, extends Test Case 5 with delete's error paths, and adds
a trailing "list" to Test Case 5 so its "no task is added as a
result" claim is actually checked against output rather than assumed.
Ran the test-ui skill; all 6 test cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot class from Duke/BOT to Bot
commitResults.messageBody:
Duke.java was renamed to Bot.java earlier but never actually renamed;
this fixes that and also settles on "Bot" (proper-name casing) over
the all-caps "BOT" used in between, since it reads as a name rather
than an acronym. Updates every reference: the class/printed name,
test/ui-test-plan.md, the test-ui skill, and both README files.

Rebuilt and reran all 6 test-ui-plan test cases; all pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save tasks to ./data/bot.txt after every change (write path)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds Task#toSaveFormat(), implemented by Todo/Deadline/Event, and a new
Storage class that serializes the task list to a pipe-separated line
per task (e.g. "T | 1 | read book"). Bot now calls Storage.save()
after every mutating command (todo, deadline, event, mark, unmark,
delete), creating ./data if needed. This is the write half of Level 7
save/load; loading the file back in on startup comes next.

Storage uses java.nio.file.Paths so the path is relative to the
project root and built with the correct separator on any OS, per the
Level 7 requirements. Also gitignore the generated ./data directory.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load saved tasks from ./data/bot.txt on startup (read path)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds Storage.load(), which parses the pipe-separated data file back
into Todo/Deadline/Event objects. Bot now populates the initial task
list from Storage.load() instead of always starting empty. Missing
file/folder is treated as an empty list (happy path for now); the file
not existing on a fresh machine's first run is the expected case.

Verified manually that a task added and marked done in one run of
Bot is present with the same state when a second run lists tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle corrupted data file and load-time errors (stretch goal)
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage.load() now parses each line independently: a line that doesn't
match the expected "type | done | description[...]" shape (unknown
type letter, non-0/1 done flag, missing field) is skipped rather than
crashing or discarding the whole file, and a description of what was
wrong with it (with its line number) is collected into a warnings
list. Bot prints those warnings once at startup, inside the usual
divider block, so the user can see that some saved tasks couldn't be
read, then carries on with whatever tasks did parse successfully.

An IOException while reading the file at all (as opposed to a
malformed line within it) still surfaces as a BotException, consistent
with how save() already reports disk errors.

Manually verified: a data file mixing well-formed lines with an
unknown type, a bad done flag, and a line missing fields entirely
loads the good lines and reports the bad ones without losing data or
crashing. Missing ./data folder and missing data file at first run are
both already handled (Files.exists check), per the Level 7 notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover save/load persistence in the UI test plan
commitResults.messageBody:
Bot now persists tasks to ./data/bot.txt across runs (Level 7), which
breaks the old assumption that every test case starts from a clean
in-memory slate: state can now leak between test cases via that file
unless it's handled explicitly. Update test/ui-test-plan.md's "How to
run" section and the test-ui skill to say a test case's Setup note
(default: delete ./data first) governs how the data file is prepared,
and to support test cases with multiple numbered Session blocks that
deliberately share one ./data across several separate program runs.

Add two new test cases exercising Level 7 directly:
- Test Case 7 runs two sessions sharing ./data and checks that tasks
  added/marked done in Session 1 reload with the same state in
  Session 2.
- Test Case 8 pre-seeds a data file mixing well-formed lines with an
  unknown type letter, a bad done flag, and a line missing fields, and
  checks the program reports each bad line and keeps the good ones
  instead of crashing or discarding everything (the stretch goal).

Ran the full updated plan (all 8 test cases, 9 program runs including
Test Case 7's two sessions) against the built program; every run's
output matches its expected block exactly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-7: save/load tasks to ./data/bot.txt
commitResults.messageBody:
Merges Level 7 (Save): the task list is now written to
./data/bot.txt after every change and reloaded from there on
startup, using a relative, OS-independent path built with
java.nio.file.Paths. Handles a missing ./data folder or data file on
first run (starts with an empty list) and a corrupted data file
(skips and reports malformed lines individually instead of crashing
or discarding everything). Also extends the UI test plan with
persistence and corrupted-file test cases and updates the test-ui
skill to handle them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse deadline/event dates as real dates instead of free text
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds TaskDateTime, a small wrapper around java.time.LocalDate/
LocalDateTime that accepts "yyyy-MM-dd" (date only) or "yyyy-MM-dd
HHmm" (date and 24-hour time) on input - both for user commands and
for reading the data file back - and displays them as e.g. "Oct 15
2019" or "Oct 15 2019, 2:00PM" depending on whether a time was
given. Deadline's "by" and Event's "from"/"to" now hold a
TaskDateTime instead of a String, so "deadline return book /by
2019-10-15" is understood as an actual date rather than an opaque
label, per Level 8's minimal requirement.

Storage's save/load format is updated to match (dates are written and
read in the same yyyy-MM-dd[ HHmm] shape TaskDateTime parses), and the
deadline/event usage messages now show a valid example date instead
of "Sunday"/"Mon 2pm". This changes the accepted input format for
deadline/event dates and the on-disk data format from Level 7 - not
backward compatible with old free-text dates, which is expected for a
still-early-stage course project.

Also adds the Level 8 stretch goal: a new "on <yyyy-MM-dd>" command
that lists tasks occurring on a given date (Task#occursOn, overridden
by Deadline to match its "by" date and by Event to match any date in
its "from".."to" range; Todo never matches, since it has no date).

Manually verified: adding dated deadlines/events displays them in the
new format, "on" correctly finds a deadline exactly on a date and an
event spanning across it, an invalid date string is rejected with a
clear message instead of crashing, and the data file round-trips
through save and a fresh load unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover Level 8 dates/times in the UI test plan
commitResults.messageBody:
deadline/event no longer accept arbitrary free-text dates - they now
require yyyy-MM-dd or yyyy-MM-dd HHmm - so every existing test case
using a free-text date ("Sunday", "June 6th", "Aug 6th 2pm", ...)
would fail against the current program. Update Test Cases 3, 6, and 7
to use real dates and their formatted ("Jun 06 2019", "Aug 06 2019,
2:00PM") display output, and extend Test Case 5 with an invalid-date
line for deadline, event, and the new on command, plus the updated
"don't understand" message listing on among the commands.

Add Test Case 9, dedicated to the on <yyyy-MM-dd> stretch-goal command:
checks a deadline matches only its exact date, an event matches any
date within its from..to range (including a date that's neither
endpoint), a date with nothing scheduled prints an empty list, and a
Todo (no date) never matches.

Ran the full updated plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs including
Test Case 7's two sessions) against the built program; every run's
output matches its expected block exactly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address PR review comments from @gabriel-wan
commitResults.messageBody:
- Split Bot#main() into smaller private methods (printWelcome,
  loadTasks, runCommandLoop, executeCommand, printFarewell) instead of
  one method doing startup, loading, the whole command loop, and
  teardown. Kept it plain method extraction within Bot.java rather
  than introducing separate Ui/Parser/Command classes, since that's a
  bigger restructuring than this fix warrants on its own.
- Declare the task list as List<Task> (with new ArrayList<>() as the
  implementation) instead of ArrayList<Task>, both in main and in
  saveTasks's parameter, reducing coupling to a specific List
  implementation.
- Extract the shared "lead-in line, task, new count" structure out of
  printAdded/printRemoved into a private printTaskCountUpdate helper;
  the two methods now just supply their own lead-in text.
- Rename the 1-based local variable in parseTaskIndex from index to
  taskNumber, since it only becomes a 0-based index on the final
  "return taskNumber - 1" line - the old name was misleading for
  every line before that.
- Narrow Task's description/isDone fields to private (description
  also final, since it's never reassigned after construction), adding
  protected getDescription()/isDone() accessors. Needed updating
  Todo/Deadline/Event's toSaveFormat(), which read these fields
  directly - contrary to the review comment's assumption that
  subclasses only used inherited methods, added in the Level 7 commit
  that introduced toSaveFormat(), after this review had been done.

Rebuilt and reran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program
runs) against the refactored code; every run's output is byte-for-byte
unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8: understand deadline/event dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
Merges Level 8 (Dates and Times): deadline's "/by" and event's
"/from"/"/to" are now parsed as real dates via a new TaskDateTime
wrapper around java.time.LocalDate/LocalDateTime, accepting
"yyyy-MM-dd" or "yyyy-MM-dd HHmm" and displaying as e.g.
"Oct 15 2019" or "Oct 15 2019, 6:00PM" - instead of storing
whatever text was typed. Adds the stretch goal: an "on <yyyy-MM-dd>"
command that lists tasks occurring on a given date (Task#occursOn,
matched exactly for a Deadline and by range for an Event; a Todo has
no date and never matches).

Also folds in a round of PR review fixes from @gabriel-wan on the
pre-Level-7 code: main() split into smaller private methods, the task
list typed as List<Task> instead of ArrayList<Task>, printAdded/
printRemoved's shared structure extracted into one helper,
parseTaskIndex's 1-based local renamed from index to taskNumber, and
Task's description/isDone fields narrowed to private (description also
final) with protected accessors added for the subclasses that read
them in toSaveFormat().

Updates the UI test plan's date-bearing test cases to the new
yyyy-MM-dd(HHmm) format and adds test cases for invalid-date errors
and the on command; all 9 test cases (10 program runs) pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui class for all console interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
Step 1 of making the code more OOP: moves every System.out print and
the Scanner read out of Bot into a new Ui class, so Bot no longer
knows about console formatting - it just calls e.g. ui.showAdded(...)
or ui.readCommand(). This is the first of four classes the increment
asks for (Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList); Storage already existed from
Level 7, so Ui goes first here.

Ui also absorbs the pluralisation/lead-in logic that used to live in
Bot's printAdded/printRemoved/printTaskCountUpdate helpers, since
that's about how output is worded, not about command handling.

Bot keeps its static structure and a static Ui field for now - it'll
become an instance with ui/storage/tasks fields in a later step once
Storage and TaskList are extracted too, matching the sample Duke
constructor from the increment's instructions. Doing that now, before
the other extractions, would mean restructuring Bot twice.

Ran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs) against the
refactored code; every run's output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class for task list operations
commitResults.messageBody:
Step 2 of making the code more OOP: introduces TaskList, which owns
the underlying List<Task> and every operation on it (add, delete, get,
size, mark, unmark, and tasksOn for the on command's date lookup).
Bot's executeCommand now calls e.g. tasks.mark(index) or
tasks.tasksOn(date) instead of indexing into a raw list and, for the
on command, filtering it inline - that filtering loop moves into
TaskList#tasksOn, which is a more natural home for a task-list query.

Bot still gets the tasks it prints or saves via TaskList#asList(),
which returns an unmodifiable copy - callers can read the list but
can't mutate it around TaskList's back.

Ran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs) against the
refactored code; every run's output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser class for interpreting user commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Step 3 of making the code more OOP: moves the command-word/argument
split and every parseX method (parseTaskIndex, parseTodo,
parseDeadline, parseEvent, parseOnDate) out of Bot into a new Parser
class. Parser.parseCommand(String) returns a small ParsedCommand
holder (command word + raw argument text); Bot's executeCommand still
does the switch on the command word and calls Storage/TaskList/Ui, but
no longer knows how to interpret the argument text for any individual
command.

ParsedCommand is a plain immutable class rather than a Java record:
this machine's javac is Java 11 (AGENTS.md calls for Java 25, which
isn't installed here), and records need Java 16+. A record would be
the more concise choice once run on the required Java version, but a
plain class compiles identically on both, so it's the safer choice
without a way to verify against Java 25 locally.

With this step, Bot only has main(), loadTasks(), runCommandLoop(),
executeCommand() (now just dispatch + wiring the other four classes
together), and saveTasks() left - no parsing or printing logic of its
own. Next step converts Bot itself from static methods to an instance
with ui/storage/tasks fields, matching the sample Duke constructor
from the increment's instructions.

Ran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs) against the
refactored code; every run's output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Storage instance-based, taking its file path in the constructor
commitResults.messageBody:
Step 4 of making the code more OOP: Storage's save/load/parseLine
methods become instance methods on a Storage that's constructed with
the data file's path (new Storage("data/bot.txt")), instead of static
methods on a class with the path baked in as a private constant. This
matches the sample Duke constructor from the increment's instructions
(storage = new Storage(filePath)) and means the file location is a
property of a Storage object rather than hidden inside the class -
useful if a future test wants to point Storage at a temp file instead
of the real data file.

save() now derives the parent directory to create from the given
path's own parent (dataFile.getParent()) rather than a separate
DATA_DIRECTORY constant, since the two always named the same directory
by construction anyway.

Bot creates one Storage instance (new Storage("data/bot.txt")) as a
static field for now, alongside its existing static Ui field; the next
step converts Bot itself into an instance with ui/storage/tasks fields
and a constructor, so main() just does .

Ran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs) against the
refactored code; every run's output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Convert Bot from static methods to an instance, per the sample shape
commitResults.messageBody:
Step 5 (final) of making the code more OOP: Bot now has ui/storage/
tasks instance fields set up in a constructor, a run() method with the
command loop, and a main() that's just new Bot("data/bot.txt").run() -
matching the constructor/run()/main() shape shown in the increment's
sample Duke code. Every method that used to be static and take a
List<Task>/TaskList parameter is now an instance method reading the
tasks field directly.

Found and fixed one behavioral regression while converting: doing the
task-loading and reporting any load error/corrupted-line warnings
inside the constructor - the natural first draft - printed them before
run() got to print the welcome banner, reversing the order the test
plan (and prior levels) established. Fixed by having the constructor
only build state (storing the load-error message and warning list as
fields without printing anything) and having run() print the welcome
banner first, then the load error/warnings, then start the command
loop - construction has no visible side effects, and the printed
order is back to matching the existing tests exactly.

This completes the increment: Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList are
now all separate classes with a single clear responsibility, and Bot
is reduced to wiring them together.

Ran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs) against the
final code; every run's output is byte-for-byte unchanged from before
this whole refactor.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-MoreOOP: extract Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
Merges the 'Make the code more OOP' increment: gradually extracts four
single-responsibility classes out of what used to be one big static
Bot class.

- Ui: all console output and input reading.
- TaskList: owns the task list and every add/delete/mark/date-lookup
  operation on it.
- Parser: splits a command line into a command word + arguments and
  interprets each command's argument text (task index, todo, deadline,
  event, date).
- Storage (refactored from Level 7's static utility): now instance-
  based, constructed with the data file's path rather than a hard-coded
  constant, matching the sample Duke(filePath) constructor from the
  increment's instructions.

Bot itself is now an instance built from these four collaborators via
a constructor, with a run() loop and main() { new Bot("data/bot.txt")
.run(); }, mirroring the sample Duke shape given in the increment
(class names differ - Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList/Bot rather than
Duke's originals - which the instructions explicitly allow).

Each of the five extraction steps was verified independently against
the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs) before moving to
the next; one real ordering regression (load-warning text printing
before the welcome banner) was caught this way and fixed by keeping
the constructor free of console side effects and having run() do the
printing in the right order. Final behavior is byte-for-byte identical
to before the refactor, so test/ui-test-plan.md needed no changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into packages under the bot root package
commitResults.messageBody:
Splits the previously flat src/main/java into packages, keeping
src/main/java itself as the source root:

- bot                - Bot (the entry point/orchestrator)
- bot.exception       - BotException
- bot.task            - Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskList
- bot.parser          - Parser, TaskDateTime
- bot.storage         - Storage
- bot.ui              - Ui

BotException gets its own package rather than sitting inside
bot.task, since it's thrown from parsing, storage I/O, and task-index
validation, not just task-related problems - folding it into task
would misrepresent its scope. TaskDateTime goes into bot.parser rather
than bot.task, since it's fundamentally about interpreting date/time
text, even though Deadline and Event (in bot.task) hold it as a field;
bot.ui and bot.storage each make one call into bot.parser as a result
(Ui#showTasksOnDate formats a date, Storage#parseLine re-parses a
saved date), which is a minor, deliberate exception to the general
rule that lower layers shouldn't depend on the parser.

Every moved file keeps its content unchanged apart from adding its
package declaration and the new cross-package imports this reorganization
requires; git tracked every move as a rename.

The program's entry point is now bot.Bot instead of Bot, so:
- javac needs to discover files recursively (a flat src/main/java/*.java
  glob only matched the old layout) - updated the test-ui skill and
  ui-test-plan.md's build step to .
- java needs the fully-qualified class name - updated both to
      ____________________________________________________________
 ____   ___  _____
| __ ) / _ \|_   _|
|  _ \| | | | | |
| |_) | |_| | | |
|____/ \___/  |_|
     Hello! I'm Bot.
     What can I do for you?
    ____________________________________________________________.
- Updated README.md's IntelliJ setup instructions to point at
  src/main/java/bot/Bot.java.

Ran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs) against the
reorganized code; every run's output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Packages: organize classes into packages
commitResults.messageBody:
Merges the 'organize classes into packages' increment. src/main/java
stays the source root; the previously flat set of 11 classes now sits
under a bot root package, split by responsibility:

- bot            - Bot (entry point/orchestrator)
- bot.exception  - BotException
- bot.task       - Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskList
- bot.parser     - Parser, TaskDateTime
- bot.storage    - Storage
- bot.ui         - Ui

BotException gets its own package rather than living in bot.task,
since it's thrown from parsing, storage I/O, and task-index validation
alike, not just task-specific problems. TaskDateTime goes into
bot.parser rather than bot.task despite Deadline/Event holding it as a
field, since it's fundamentally a date/time interpretation concern;
bot.ui and bot.storage each make one call into bot.parser as a
consequence (formatting a date for display, re-parsing a saved date),
a deliberate, minor exception to lower layers not depending on the
parser.

Every file kept its content unchanged apart from its new package
declaration and the cross-package imports the split requires; git
tracked every move as a rename. Build/run instructions were updated
everywhere they assumed the old flat layout (test/ui-test-plan.md,
the test-ui skill, and README.md's IntelliJ path): a flat
src/main/java/*.java glob no longer finds every file, so the build
now discovers sources recursively, and the entry point is bot.Bot
instead of Bot.

Ran the full UI test plan (9 test cases, 10 program runs) against the
reorganized code; every run's output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword (Level 9)
commitResults.messageBody:
Give users a way to find a task by searching for a keyword in the
task description.

TaskList#findByKeyword(String) returns every task whose description
contains the keyword, matched case-insensitively (so "find book"
also catches "Read Book"), keeping original list order. Parser gains
parseFindKeyword, rejecting an empty/missing keyword the same way
other commands reject missing arguments. Ui#showMatchingTasks prints
the results under "Here are the matching tasks in your list:",
reusing the same numbered-list format as list/on. Bot wires a new
"find" case into its command switch and adds find to the
unrecognized-command usage message.

Added Test Case 10 to the UI test plan and verified all 10 test cases
build and behave as expected, apart from 3 failures in Test Cases 2,
6, and 9 that are a pre-existing, unrelated issue (TaskDateTime's
formatters don't pin a Locale, so the AM/PM case in event times
depends on the JVM's default locale/version - this machine's JDK
upgrade to 25 changed it from "PM" to "pm" for the exact same
locale) - confirmed the diffs only touch event time-of-day text, none
of it related to find.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaDoc comments to classes and methods (A-JavaDoc)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add JavaDoc comments to the code.

Documents every previously-undocumented public/protected class,
constructor, method, and field across the codebase: Task's
constructor/getStatusIcon/markAsDone/markAsNotDone/toString, Todo's
constructor/toString, Deadline's constructor/toString/occursOn/by
field, Event's constructor/toString/occursOn/from and to fields,
TaskList's add/get/size/mark/unmark, TaskDateTime#toLocalDate,
BotException's constructor, Storage's constructor, Parser's
parseTodo/parseDeadline/parseEvent/parseOnDate and
ParsedCommand#commandWord/arguments, and Bot#main. Ui.java already had
full coverage from when each method was first written and needed no
changes.

Went with the increment's stretch goal (all non-private members, not
just half) since it costs little extra here and matches AGENTS.md's
existing preference for explaining nontrivial behavior. Verified with
a script scanning every public/protected declaration for a preceding
Javadoc comment: none remain undocumented.

Doc-only change - rebuilt and manually smoke-tested (todo/list/bye);
behavior is unchanged, so the existing UI test plan needed no updates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
This project must follow the SE-EDU Java coding standard for A-CodingStandard.

Without a saved reference, every future session would need to
re-fetch and re-derive the same rules from
se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html, and could
drift on details like the required switch-statement indentation or
when Javadoc may be omitted.

Let's capture the standard's naming, layout, statement, and comment
rules as a project skill, so it can be loaded before writing or
reviewing any Java code in this repository, now and in future
sessions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-git-standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
This project must follow SE-EDU's Git commit message and branch name
conventions from now on.

Without a saved reference, commit messages could drift back to
non-imperative subjects, missing bodies on non-trivial commits, or
inconsistent branch names, since there'd be nothing to check new
commits against session to session.

Let's capture the subject-line rules (length, mood, capitalization,
no trailing period), the body's what/why focus and suggested shape,
and the branch-naming convention as a project skill, so it can be
loaded before proposing or creating any commit or branch name.

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Mandate SE-EDU Java and Git standards
commitResults.messageBody:
Java code and commit messages in this repository were following no
single documented standard, so consistency depended on whoever
happened to be writing at the time.

The seedu-java-coding-standard and seedu-git-standard skills now exist
to define that standard, but a skill existing isn't the same as it
being required reading.

Let's add explicit requirements to load and follow
seedu-java-coding-standard before touching any .java file, and
seedu-git-standard before proposing or creating any commit message, so
both are treated as mandatory rather than optional references.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tweak code to comply with the SE-EDU Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
The codebase didn't yet follow seedu-java-coding-standard: both
switch statements used IDE-default indentation (case aligned with
switch, not indented one level in), one local variable holding a
collection had a non-plural name, and several public
classes/constructors/methods lacked the required Javadoc header
comment.

Let's,
* reindent Bot#executeCommand's and Storage#parseLine's switch
  statements so each case is one level in from switch, matching the
  standard's required form
* rename TaskList#tasksOn's local matching to matchingTasks, per the
  naming rule that a variable holding a collection should be plural
* add Javadoc to every public class/constructor/method that lacked
  one, applying the standard's own exemptions (getters/setters and
  overriding methods whose parent Javadoc already applies as-is are
  left uncommented)

Six lines already sit a little past the 110-char soft limit; all stay
under the 120-char hard limit, which the standard explicitly allows,
so they're left as-is rather than force-wrapped.

Rebuilt and reran the full UI test plan; all 9 test cases pass apart
from 3 that fail only on a pre-existing, unrelated locale issue
(TaskDateTime's AM/PM case depends on the JVM's default locale/
version) already present before this change.
